learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how energy travels through space without moving matter! Understand the difference between light and sound, how interference works, and the secret behind musical instruments.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Waves are a disturbance that transport energy without transporting matter. Mechanical waves (like sound or water waves) absolutely require a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. They cannot travel through a vacuum.

In Transverse waves (like plucking a guitar string), particles vibrate perpendicular (up and down) to the wave's direction. In Longitudinal waves (like sound in air), particles vibrate parallel (back and forth) creating compressions and rarefactions.

A traveling wave is represented by $y(x,t) = A \sin(kx - \omega t)$. It shows that the displacement '$y$' depends on both position '$x$' and time '$t$'. '$k$' is the angular wave number ($2\pi/\lambda$).

When two or more waves overlap, their displacements just add up! This creates 'Interference'. If peaks meet peaks, the wave gets bigger (Constructive). If peaks meet troughs, they cancel out (Destructive).

When two identical waves travel in opposite directions, they form a 'Standing Wave' (looks like it's vibrating in place, with fixed zero-points called Nodes). When two waves of slightly different frequencies overlap, they create a pulsing volume effect called 'Beats'.

fun_activity.title: 🍷 The Singing Wine Glass
fun_activity.instructions: Dip your finger in water and gently rub it in a continuous circle around the rim of a thin glass goblet (like a wine glass). After a few seconds, the glass will 'sing' a loud, clear note! You are creating 'Standing Waves' inside the glass via resonance.

exam_tips: 📌 Know the difference between Open and Closed Organ Pipes. An open pipe produces all harmonics (f, 2f, 3f...). A closed pipe only produces ODD harmonics (f, 3f, 5f...).
📌 The Beat Frequency formula is simply the difference between the two frequencies: $f_{beat} = |f_1 - f_2|$.
📌 Be able to identify the amplitude, wavelength, and frequency directly from a given wave equation.
quick_recap: ⭐ Sound waves travel much faster in solids (like steel) than in air because the molecules are packed tighter and transfer the energy faster.
⭐ Distance between two consecutive Nodes (or Antinodes) in a standing wave is always $\lambda / 2$.
⭐ A progressive wave transports energy from one place to another; a standing wave traps the energy in a confined region.
